sources_considered.why: Contemporaneous evaluation of action-taking agents on workplace tasks including email and calendars.
Verifies that the evaluated version was public on May 1, before the post.
Original, pre-publication version of a broad computer-assistant evaluation.
Shows partial browser-agent success, but WorkBench provides more directly relevant evidence about email, calendars and actions across domains.

evidence_items.locator: Concluding discussion after limitations; results in Section 4
evidence_items.explanation: The benchmark evaluates 690 tasks involving tools and database changes, including email and scheduling. Its low overall success and documented harmful mistakes support limited evidence for dependable assistance.

Across 369 real computer tasks, the strongest evaluated model achieved 12.24% success compared with 72.36% for humans. This provides broader evidence of a large reliability gap in computer assistance.

WorkBench also demonstrates genuine progress: its GPT-4 agent completed some tasks combining tools across domains. This is evidence toward future assistants, though its reported 40% success on those tasks does not demonstrate dependable assistance.

unresolved_gaps: No numerical boundary separates little evidence from substantial evidence.
These evaluations do not exhaust every product or demonstration available at publication.
They measure present capabilities, not the probability of eventual success.
